note: Generated by the Browser Workflow server (scripts/sync-tools.ts): edit the tools there, not this file.
instructions:
browser-workflow creates, runs and fixes browser-automation workflows (JSON step graphs run in a real Chrome).
Always check setup first: before any other tool in a conversation, call `get_account` (it shows the user nothing). Its answer ends with "Setup: finished" or "Setup: not finished". When it is not finished, call `setup`, end your reply with one short line and wait: do nothing else, whatever the user asked for, until they have finished it in the widget (it tells you when), then go on with what they asked. Do the same whenever a tool says setup is not finished. Once you have seen "Setup: finished" in this conversation, you need not check again.
Never change a workflow directly: use import_workflow (a file the user gave), propose_workflow (a new one) or propose_change (edits/fixes). The user confirms in the widget.
To build or fix a workflow, first read the format with get_step_schema, explore the site with the page_* inspector tools (take_snapshot shows the page structure), then propose.
Every lookup has two tools that answer you with the same text: a silent one (read_workflows, get_workflow, get_history, read_runs, get_run, get_step, get_run_data, get_failure, get_account), which shows the user nothing, and one that also puts a widget in the chat (list_workflows, show_workflow, show_history, list_runs, show_run, show_step, show_run_data, show_failure, show_account).
While you are still working (you need the answer to decide or do something next), always use the silent one. Never call a tool that shows a widget to check something.
For your final answer, when what the user asked for is what a widget shows (their workflows, a workflow, a run, a failure, the extracted items, the history, their account), call the tool that shows it instead of writing it out, and go straight to it when that is all they asked: do not call the silent one first. Then add one short line, and do not repeat in text what the widget shows. A single fact ("how many workflows do I have", "when did it last run") is answered in a sentence, with the silent tool and no widget.
browser_settings shows a widget too: only when the user asked to change how their browser is reached.
One widget per reply. After a tool that shows a widget where the user has something to do (setup, link_computer, import_workflow, propose_workflow, propose_change, a run form, or any list_* or show_* tool), end your reply with one short line and wait for the user. Never show two widgets in one reply.
When a run fails, call get_failure (screenshot, error, HTML near the target) before proposing a fix; pass runId to propose_change.
Reply in the user's language. The widgets are in English or Vietnamese, one language per account. `get_account` says which, or that none is chosen yet: then call `set_language` once, before any tool that shows a widget, with the language the user writes in (judge by their own words, not by a prompt this app wrote for them; `vi` for Vietnamese, `en` for anything else), and tell them in one short line which language you will use and that they can ask you to open their account settings to change it. Once a language is chosen, never change it yourself: when the user wants another one, call `show_account`: they pick it there, or on the account page its button opens.
Runs use the user's own Chrome through the Browser Workflow app on their computer (started by the AI app it is installed in), which also provides the page_* inspector tools and a `bridge_status` tool. The `get_account` check at the start also says whether it is connected (its answer has `Browser bridge: connected` or `not connected`). Not connected comes before `setup` and before building, inspecting or running anything, and it is one of two cases that you tell apart by your own tools. If you have a `bridge_status` tool (the app's; look for it, its full name may be longer), the app is installed and only needs linking: call it; when it shows a pairing code, call `link_computer` with that code, and the user clicks one button. Do this instead of `setup`, and never tell the user to install the app in this case. Only if you do not have `bridge_status` is the app not installed: then call `setup`, whose widget says how to install it in the app the user is in. When the user says they installed it, look for `bridge_status` again and link the computer. Never describe install steps of your own, and never ask the user to copy a code or a token.
Those runs are saved on the user's computer by the app, so reading a past run (get_run, get_failure, read_runs, get_run_data, and the tools that show them) also needs it connected.
People can use this without signing up (an anonymous account). When a tool answers that an account is needed, the widget shows a "Create account" button that opens a page for it: point the user to that button, and never ask for a username or password in the chat. If you have an `open_login_page` tool (the app's) and the user wants to log in or create an account, call it: it opens the login page in their Chrome, their computer is linked to the account once they log in or sign up, and what they made before stays theirs.

tools.name: setup
tools.title: Set up browser-workflow
tools.description: Shows the setup widget, where the user connects a browser, then imports or creates a first workflow. Call it for new users or when a tool says setup is not finished, alone: no other widget in the same reply.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.title: List workflows
tools.description: Lists the user's workflows for them, in a widget where they can open or run one (all of them, or a search). Use it whenever the user asks for their workflows, and do not write the list out yourself. Only while you are still working and need the list for yourself, use read_workflows, which shows nothing.

query.description: Filter by name, host or description

tools.name: show_workflow
tools.title: Get workflow
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user one workflow (steps, variables, version); they can run it or ask for edits there. Use it when the user asks about one workflow, instead of writing its steps out. To read its definition for your own work, use get_workflow, which shows nothing.

tools.name: get_step_schema
tools.title: Get workflow format
tools.description: How to build workflows, plus the JSON Schema of the format and every step type. Read this before drafting or changing workflows.

tools.name: import_workflow
tools.title: Import workflow
tools.description: Validate a workflow JSON file (e.g. one the user attached) and show an import preview. Nothing is saved until the user confirms in the widget.

tools.name: propose_workflow
tools.title: Propose new workflow
tools.description: Show a drafted workflow (format: get_step_schema) to the user for review. The user saves it, or saves and test-runs it, from the widget.

workflow.description: Workflow JSON: id, name, pageUrl?, description, steps[], environmentVariableSchema?

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.title: Run workflow
tools.description: Start a run from the first step. If required inputs are missing the user gets a form. Returns a runId; the widget shows live progress.

browser.description: Override the default browser mode for this run

stopAfterStepId.description: Stop after this step (to test a change without running everything)

form.description: Widget use: show the input form even if all inputs have defaults

tools.name: show_run
tools.title: Get run status
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user a run: its status and per-step progress, live while it runs. Use it when the user asks how a run went, instead of writing it out. To check a run for your own work, use get_run, which shows nothing.

tools.name: show_failure
tools.title: Get run failure
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user the failure of a run (failing step, error, screenshot). Use it when the user asks why a run failed and you are not proposing a fix in this reply. To read what was captured before proposing a fix, use get_failure, which shows nothing.

tools.name: propose_change
tools.title: Propose a change
tools.description: Propose edits to a workflow (a fix for a failed run, or a change the user asked for on a step). Shows a before/after with a one-line reason; the user applies & tests it (re-run from the start up to the changed step) or discards it. Nothing changes until the user applies it.

reason.description: One sentence, in the user's language: what was wrong and what changes

runId.description: The failed run this fixes, if any

step.description: update: fields to change (action is merged); add: the full new step

afterStepId.description: add: insert after this step (default: at the end). Remember to update nextStepId links.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.title: List runs
tools.description: Lists the past runs of a workflow for the user, newest first, in a widget where they can open one. Use it whenever the user asks for past runs, and do not write them out yourself. Only while you are still working and need them for yourself, use read_runs, which shows nothing.

tools.name: show_step
tools.title: Get step in a run
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user what one step did in one run (state, output or error, screenshot). Use it when the user asks what a step did. To read it for your own work, use get_step, which shows nothing.

tools.name: show_run_data
tools.title: Get extracted data
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user the table of items a run extracted, with downloads. Use it when the user asks for the data or results of a run, instead of writing a table. To read the items for your own work, use get_run_data, which shows nothing and gives every item.

tools.name: show_history
tools.title: Workflow versions
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user the version history of a workflow; they can restore an older version there. Use it when the user asks what changed or wants an older version back. To read it for your own work, use get_history, which shows nothing.

tools.name: browser_settings
tools.title: Browser settings
tools.description: Only when the user asked to change how their browser is reached: shows the browser connection settings (the user's Chrome, a remote DevTools endpoint, or a new Chrome).

tools.name: show_account
tools.title: Account
tools.description: For your final answer, not while you are still working. Shows the user who they are, their plan and one button: create an account or log in, upgrade, or open their account page, where their usage, password and language are. Use it when the user asks about their account, plan, usage or settings, and do not write the numbers out beside it. To read them for your own work, use get_account, which shows nothing.

tools.name: read_workflows
tools.title: Read workflows
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. The saved workflows and the examples: id, name, version, number of steps, last run.

query.description: Filter by name, host or description

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.title: Read workflow
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. The full definition of a workflow as JSON (steps, variables, version). Read it before proposing a change.

tools.name: get_history
tools.title: Read workflow versions
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. The versions of a workflow: when, by whom, and what changed.

tools.name: read_runs
tools.title: Read runs
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. Past runs of a workflow, newest first: run id, time, version, status, items.

tools.name: get_run
tools.title: Read run
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. A run's status and the state of each step. Use it to check a run you started.

tools.name: get_step
tools.title: Read step in a run
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. What one step did in one run: state, duration, URL, output or error, variables before it, and its screenshot.

tools.name: get_run_data
tools.title: Read extracted data
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. The items a run extracted, one JSON object per line, a part at a time: the answer says how to get the next part.

tools.name: get_failure
tools.title: Read run failure
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. Everything captured when a run failed: failing step and its definition, error, URL, console errors, variables, HTML near the target element, and a screenshot.

tools.name: get_account
tools.title: Read account
tools.description: For your own work, while you are still working: answers with text and shows the user nothing. Plan, usage against the limits, where runs are stored, whether the app on the user's computer is connected, and whether setup is finished. Call it first in a conversation, before any other tool.

tools.name: set_language
tools.title: Set language
tools.description: Sets the language of the widgets (English or Vietnamese) to the one the user writes in, and shows nothing. Only when get_account says no language is chosen yet, and before any tool that shows a widget. It changes nothing once a language is chosen: the user changes it in their account settings.

lang.description: vi when the user writes in Vietnamese, en for anything else

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.title: Delete workflow
tools.description: Delete a workflow, all its versions and runs. Only when the user clearly asks.

tools.name: show_workflows
tools.title: List workflows
tools.description: The workflow library, for the widget.

tools.name: show_runs
tools.title: Workflow runs
tools.description: The past runs of a workflow, for the widget.

tools.name: ui_confirm_import
tools.title: Confirm import
tools.description: Save an import preview.

tools.name: ui_save_draft
tools.title: Save draft
tools.description: Save a proposed workflow, under the name the user typed.

tools.name: ui_test_draft
tools.title: Test a draft
tools.description: Run a proposed workflow without saving it.

tools.name: ui_apply_change
tools.title: Apply change
tools.description: Apply a proposed change and test it.

tools.name: ui_discard_change
tools.title: Discard change
tools.description: Discard a proposed change.

tools.name: ui_restore_version
tools.title: Restore version
tools.description: Restore an older version.

tools.name: ui_resume_manual
tools.title: Resume run
tools.description: Resume after a manual step.

tools.name: ui_stop_run
tools.title: Stop run
tools.description: Stop a run.

tools.name: ui_check_browser
tools.title: Check browser
tools.description: Test the browser connection.

tools.name: ui_save_browser
tools.title: Save browser
tools.description: Save browser settings.

tools.name: ui_get_screenshot
tools.title: Get screenshot
tools.description: A step screenshot for the widget.

tools.name: ui_set_language
tools.title: Set language
tools.description: Widget language.

tools.name: ui_sign_in
tools.title: Sign in
tools.description: Sign in.

tools.name: ui_finish_setup
tools.title: Finish setup
tools.description: Mark setup as done.

tools.name: ui_new_bridge_token
tools.title: New bridge token
tools.description: Create a new bridge token (replaces the old one).

tools.name: ui_account_page
tools.title: Account page
tools.description: A one-time address of the account page: plan, usage and settings.

tools.name: ui_account_link
tools.title: Create account
tools.description: A one-time page where an anonymous account picks a username and password.

tools.name: link_computer
tools.title: Link this computer
tools.description: Links the user's computer to their account. Pass the pairing code the Browser Workflow app shows in its bridge_status tool. The user is shown a "Link this computer" button and nothing is linked until they click it.

code.description: The pairing code from the app's bridge_status, like ABCD-EFGH

tools.name: ui_confirm_link
tools.title: Confirm link
tools.description: The user clicked "Link this computer".
